To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electron mobility in semi-metal quantum wells is determined by the well width, the hole concentration and the electron concentration.
electron mobility in n-type HgCdTe QW is determined by the competition of the screening effect and the electron concentration.
the electron mobility in HgCdTe semi-metal quantum wells is limited by electron–phonon, electron–electron and electron–hole scattering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electron transport in semi-metal HcCdTe quantum wells.
the influence of the well width on the carrier concentration and the electron mobility in the intrinsic and doped semi-metal Hg1-xCdxTe quantum wells.
the electron mobility dependence on the well thickness and carrier concentration in semi-metal HgLxTe1-x quantum wells at liquid nitrogen temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron mobility in n-type HgCdTe QW is mainly limited by the scattering on holes.

the mobility of 2DEG in the semi-metal quantum wells can be described in the model of the screened electron–phonon and electron–impurity scattering, and that the mobility of the holes in the quantum well can be described by the model of the unscreened electron–hole scattering.
electron mobility in n-type semi-metal quantum well is limited by the ionized impurities, and in p-type quantum wells it is limited by the electron–hole scattering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron mobility in HgCdTe semi-metal QWs is limited by the electron scattering on holes and on charged impurities in a broad range of QW widths.
electron mobility in n-type HgCdTe semi-metallic quantum wells is determined by the well width and by the concentration of impurities.

the electron mobility in the semi-metal HgTe/CdTe quantum well with 10 nm well width is about 10 ^{5}  cm ^{2} /(V s), while in a semi-metal Hg _{0.3} Cd _{0.7} Te/CdTe quantum wells with 10 mm well width the mobility is about 10 cm ^{2 } /(V s) at 77 K.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron mobility in semi-metal quantum wells is strongly affected by the well width and the electron density.
in the narrow quantum wells (less than 20 nm) the electron mobility is limited by electron–phonon interaction.
electron mobility in semi-metal quantum wells is strongly dependent on the well width.
